hook: The First Emperor, who united China and was buried with an army of clay.

pages.x: Ying Zheng became king of Qin, a tough state in western China, in 246 BC, at 13. China was then split into seven warring kingdoms. As a young man he took power from the regent who had run the state for him, and banished his own mother.

In 227 BC an assassin, Jing Ke, came to court offering a map of land to hand over. As the map was unrolled, a poisoned dagger appeared inside. The king leapt up and ran round a pillar, struggling to draw his long sword, until a courtier shouted "Put it on your back!" He drew it and cut the assassin down.

Between 230 and 221 BC Qin conquered the other six kingdoms one by one. Ying Zheng took a new title, Shi Huangdi, "First Emperor". The name of his state, Qin, said "chin", may be where the word China comes from.
He made the whole empire use one style of writing, one set of weights and measures, one coin, and even one width for cart axles.
pages.fx: A single written script let people across China read the same books for 2,200 years, even when they spoke different languages.

pages.x: He joined up the walls of the old kingdoms into one long wall against the nomads of the north. Hundreds of thousands of soldiers and convicts were forced to build it, and so many died that it was called the longest cemetery on Earth. Most of the wall seen today was built much later.

To silence critics, he had books of history and philosophy burned in 213 BC, sparing only books on medicine, farming and fortune-telling. Tradition says 460 scholars were buried alive. Afraid of death, he also sent ships to find a potion of eternal life, and drank medicines containing mercury.
pages.img: Burning of books and burying of scholars

pages.x: He died in 210 BC and was buried near Xi'an, guarded by more than 8,000 life-size clay soldiers, each with its own face, with horses and chariots. Farmers digging a well found them in 1974. His tomb itself has never been opened; an ancient historian wrote that it holds rivers of mercury.
The First Emperor was cruel, but he created a united China with one script, one law and one system of government that lasted, through all its dynasties, for over 2,000 years.
pts: First emperor of a united China
Made one script, coin and measure for all China
